items.q: What is the car's kinetic energy at 10 m/s? Give the value and its unit.

mistakes.why: Value: that is the mass times the speed. Kinetic energy squares the speed and takes half: ½(1200 kg)(10 m/s)².

items.q: How does the car's kinetic energy at 20 m/s compare with its kinetic energy at 10 m/s?
options: 4 times as large
2 times as large
8 times as large
The same, since the mass is the same

items.q: By how much does the car's kinetic energy increase when it speeds up from 10 m/s to 20 m/s? Give the value and its unit.

mistakes.why: Value: that is ½m(Δv)². The change in K is ½mv_f² − ½mv_i²: square each speed first, then subtract.
Value: that is the kinetic energy at 20 m/s. Subtract the kinetic energy at 10 m/s to get the change.

items.q: With the same braking force, the car at 10 m/s stops in a distance d. In what distance does it stop from 20 m/s?
options: 2d
4d
d

items.q: The car turns around and drives west at 20 m/s instead of east. Taking east as positive, what is its kinetic energy?
options: −2.4 × 10⁵ J, because the velocity is negative
Zero, because west cancels east
2.4 × 10⁵ J, the same as driving east
1.2 × 10⁵ J, half the eastward value

items.q: What is the tennis ball's kinetic energy, in joules?

mistakes.why: Value: that multiplies the mass by the speed. Kinetic energy is ½mv², with the speed squared.

items.q: How does the bowling ball's kinetic energy compare with the tennis ball's?
options: The bowling ball's is 100 times larger
The tennis ball's is 10 times larger
The bowling ball's is 10 times larger
They are equal

items.q: Which comparison of the sprinter and the cyclist is correct?
options: The sprinter has about twice as much
The cyclist has more, because the cyclist has more mass
They have about the same kinetic energy
The sprinter has about 1.5 times as much

items.q: How fast would the cyclist and bike (80. kg) have to move to have the same kinetic energy as the sprinter? Answer in m/s.

mistakes.why: Value: that divides K by m. Solve K = ½mv² for v: v = √(2K/m).
Value: you left out the 2. Solving K = ½mv² gives v = √(2K/m).

items.q: Which combination of SI base units is the same as a joule?
options: kg·m/s
kg·m²/s²
kg·m/s²
kg·m²/s

items.q: A student finds that a 2.0 kg cart moving left at 3.0 m/s has a kinetic energy of −9.0 J. What went wrong?
options: Nothing: leftward motion has negative kinetic energy
The ½ was left out; it should be −4.5 J
K cannot be negative; it is +9.0 J
The speed should not be squared; it is −3.0 J

items.q: A passenger sits still in a train that moves at 25 m/s along a straight track. Which statement about the passenger's kinetic energy is correct?
options: It is the same measured from the train and from the ground
It is zero in both frames because the passenger is sitting still
It is large in both frames because the train is moving
Zero in the train's frame, large in the ground's

items.q: A 0.40 kg cart speeds up from 1.5 m/s to 2.5 m/s. By how much does its kinetic energy change, in joules?

mistakes.why: Value: that is ½m(Δv)². Compute ½mv² at each speed, then subtract.
Value: that is the final kinetic energy. Subtract the starting kinetic energy.

items.q: A crate moving at 3.0 m/s has 54 J of kinetic energy. What is its mass, in kg?

mistakes.why: Value: the speed must be squared. m = 2K/v² = 2(54 J)/(3.0 m/s)².

items.q: A cart moving east at 3.0 m/s is stopped, then pushed west until it moves west at 3.0 m/s. Take east as positive. Compare the end with the start.

variables.name: The x-component of the cart's velocity

items.q: A truck has 3 times the mass of a car and moves at half the car's speed. What is the ratio of the truck's kinetic energy to the car's?
Two 1.0 kg carts move toward each other, one east at 2.0 m/s and one west at 2.0 m/s. What is the kinetic energy of the two-cart system?
options: Zero, because the motions are opposite

items.q: How much work does the rope do on the crate over the 4.00 m? Give the value and its unit.

mistakes.why: Value: that uses the whole rope force. Only the part along the displacement does work: F d cos 30°.
Value: that uses sin 30°. The angle is measured from the displacement, so use cos 30°.

items.q: How much work does kinetic friction do on the crate over the 4.00 m, in joules? Include the sign.
How much work do the normal force and the gravitational force do on the crate over the 4.00 m?
options: Zero each: each is perpendicular to the displacement
+696 J by the normal force and −784 J by gravity
Zero by the normal force, −784 J by gravity
Both positive, since both act on the crate while it moves

items.q: What is the net work done on the crate over the 4.00 m, in joules?

mistakes.why: Value: that adds the friction work as if it were positive. Friction does negative work, so subtract it.
Value: that uses the whole rope force (180 J). The rope does F d cos 30° = 156 J.

items.q: The crate starts from rest. How fast is it moving after the 4.00 m, in m/s?

mistakes.why: Value: that uses only the rope's work. The change in kinetic energy equals the net work, so include friction.

items.q: How much work does the band do on the cart from x = 0 to x = 0.40 m, in joules?

mistakes.why: Value: that treats the force as 12 N the whole way. The work is the area under the graph, and the force falls after 0.10 m.
Value: that treats the whole area as one triangle. From 0 to 0.10 m it is a rectangle.

items.q: How fast is the 0.60 kg cart moving at x = 0.40 m, in m/s?

mistakes.why: Value: that uses 4.8 J, a constant 12 N force. Use the area under the graph, 3.0 J.

items.q: What happens to the cart's speed between x = 0.40 m and x = 0.50 m?
options: It decreases, because the band no longer pushes
It stays the same, because the band does no work there
It increases, because the cart is still moving forward
It drops to zero, because the force is zero

items.q: Over which 0.10 m interval does the band do the most work on the cart?
options: Each of the four intervals, equally

items.q: A worker lowers a 15 kg box onto the floor at constant speed. What sign is the work done by the worker on the box?
options: Positive, because the worker is making an effort
Zero, because the speed is constant
Positive, because the box moves
Negative, because the push opposes the motion

items.q: A ball on a string moves in a horizontal circle at constant speed. Which is the best explanation of why its speed does not change?
options: The string's force is perpendicular to the velocity, so it does no work
The string's force is zero, because the ball moves at constant speed
The string does positive work that is canceled by negative work from gravity
The ball has no acceleration, so nothing does work

items.q: A 3.0 kg ball falls 2.5 m. How much work does the gravitational force do on the ball, in joules? Use g = 9.8 m/s².
A rope pulls a crate up a straight ramp at constant speed. What is the net work done on the crate?
options: Positive, because the rope pulls the crate uphill
Zero, because its kinetic energy does not change
Negative, because gravity opposes the motion
It equals the crate's weight times the height of the ramp

items.q: A 0.17 kg puck slides at 6.0 m/s onto rough ice, where a 0.50 N friction force slows it. How far does it slide before stopping, in meters?

mistakes.why: Value: that divides mass times speed by the force. Use the work-energy theorem: −f d = 0 − ½mv².

items.q: A crate is dragged 5.0 m east and then 5.0 m back west to where it started. Kinetic friction from the floor has size f the whole time. What total work does friction do on the crate?
options: Zero, because the crate ends where it started

items.q: A constant force pushes a cart along its motion. If the force is doubled and the distance is halved, what happens to the work done by the force?
options: It doubles
It is halved
It is four times as large
It stays the same

items.q: On a graph of the force along the direction of motion against position, what represents the work done by the force?
options: The area between the graph and the position axis
The slope of the graph
The largest force times the total time
The height of the graph at the final position

items.q: Take a sled as the system. A rope outside the system pulls it forward and does +40 J of work on it. What does this tell you?
options: 40 J of energy left the sled
40 J of energy entered the sled
The sled's speed is certain to increase
The rope gained 40 J

items.q: Take the floor as the zero of gravitational potential energy. What is the gravitational potential energy of the book-Earth system with the book on the shelf? Give the value and its unit.
Now take the table top as the zero. What is the gravitational potential energy of the book-Earth system with the book on the shelf, in joules?

mistakes.why: Value: 0.80 m is the table's height above the floor. Measure from the new zero: 1.50 m − 0.80 m = 0.70 m.
Value: that is measured from the floor. With the table top as zero, the height is 0.70 m.

items.q: The book is moved from the shelf to the table top. How does the change in the system's gravitational potential energy depend on the choice of zero?
options: It is about −14 J for either choice of zero
It is −29 J with the floor as zero and −14 J with the table as zero
It is zero with the table as zero, because the book ends at zero
It is +14 J, because the book moves to a new height

items.q: A student writes "the book has 29 J of potential energy." Which correction is best?
options: The potential energy belongs to the shelf, which holds the book up
The potential energy belongs to the book-Earth system, not to the book alone
The value should be 29 N, because it comes from the weight
The book has 29 J of kinetic energy instead

items.q: The book falls from the shelf to the floor. With the floor as zero, which pair describes the work done on the book by the gravitational force and the change in the book-Earth system's potential energy?
options: W = −29 J and ΔU_g = +29 J
W = +29 J and ΔU_g = +29 J
W = +29 J and ΔU_g = −29 J
W = 0 and ΔU_g = −29 J

items.q: When the compression doubles from 0.020 m to 0.040 m, the stored energy
options: doubles
stays the same, because the spring is the same
increases by 0.10 J
becomes 4 times as large

items.q: Use the 0.080 m row to find the spring constant, in N/m.

mistakes.why: Value: you left out the 2. From U_s = ½k(Δx)², k = 2U_s/(Δx)².
Value: the compression must be squared: k = 2U_s/(Δx)².

items.q: How much energy does the same spring store when compressed 0.10 m, in joules?

mistakes.why: Value: the compression must be squared: ½k(Δx)² = ½(500 N/m)(0.10 m)².

items.q: The student wants a straight-line graph whose slope gives k. What should be plotted?
options: U_s against (Δx)²; the slope is ½k
U_s against Δx; the slope is k
U_s against (Δx)²; the slope is k
Δx against U_s; the slope is 1/k

items.q: Which of these forces is nonconservative?
options: The force from an ideal spring on a block
Kinetic friction from a rough floor on a sliding box
The gravitational force from Earth on a ball
The gravitational force between two distant asteroids

items.q: A 1.0 kg ball is carried from the floor to a 2.0 m high shelf, once straight up and once along a long winding staircase. Compare the work done on the ball by the gravitational force on the two paths.
options: It is larger on the staircase, which is longer
It is zero on the staircase, because most of the motion is horizontal
It is the same on both paths
It is larger on the straight path, which is steeper

items.q: A 500. kg satellite orbits 7.0 × 10⁶ m from Earth's center. Earth's mass is 5.97 × 10²⁴ kg and G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg². What is the gravitational potential energy of the satellite-Earth system, with zero at infinite separation? Give the value and its unit.

mistakes.why: Value: that divides by r². Gravitational force goes as 1/r², but the potential energy goes as 1/r: U_G = −Gm₁m₂/r.
Value: mgh only works near Earth's surface, where g is constant. Far away, use U_G = −Gm₁m₂/r.

items.q: A space probe moves farther from Earth. With zero at infinite separation, what happens to the gravitational potential energy of the probe-Earth system?
options: It decreases, because the gravitational force gets weaker
It stays the same, because the masses do not change
It becomes more negative, approaching negative infinity
It increases toward zero, becoming less negative

items.q: Near Earth's surface, a crate is raised to twice its original height above the floor (floor as zero). The gravitational potential energy of the crate-Earth system becomes
options: 2 times as large
4 times as large
√2 times as large
unchanged, because the mass is the same

items.q: A ball sits at the bottom of a pit, 3.0 m below the ground. A student puts the zero of gravitational potential energy at ground level. Which statement is correct?
options: U_g has to be positive, so the zero should move to the pit floor
U_g is negative, and that is fine: only changes in U_g have physical meaning
U_g is positive, because the ball is 3.0 m from the zero
U_g is zero, because the ball is at rest

items.q: An ideal spring compressed 0.020 m is compressed further, to 0.040 m. Predict how each quantity changes.

variables.name: The elastic potential energy of the system
The size of the spring's force on the block

items.q: How fast is the block moving at B, in m/s?

mistakes.why: Value: you left out the 2. From mgΔy = ½mv², v = √(2gΔy).

items.q: How fast is the block moving at C, in m/s?

mistakes.why: Value: 2.0 m is C's height above B. The block has dropped 6.0 m − 2.0 m = 4.0 m from A.
Value: you added the heights. The drop from A to C is 6.0 m − 2.0 m = 4.0 m.

items.q: Which describes an energy bar chart for the block-track-Earth system at C, with the zero of U_g at B?
options: K is twice U_g, and K + U_g equals the U_g bar at A
K and U_g are equal, each one half of the total energy
U_g is twice K, because C is high on the track
K is twice U_g, and the total is less than at A

items.q: A 4.0 kg block is released from A instead. How does its speed at C compare with the 2.0 kg block's?
options: It is twice as large
It is the same
It is √2 times as large
It is half as large

items.q: Now take the block alone as the system. Which statement is correct as it slides from A to B?
options: The block alone has gravitational potential energy that turns into kinetic energy
The block's energy is constant, because the track is frictionless and nothing slows it
It has just kinetic energy, and Earth's pull, now external, does positive work on it
The normal force from the track does the work that speeds the block up

items.q: What is the mechanical energy (K + U_g) of the skier-Earth system at the middle point, in joules?

mistakes.why: Value: that is U_g alone. Add the kinetic energy, ½(60.0 kg)(12.0 m/s)².
Value: that is K alone. Add U_g = mg(10.0 m).

items.q: How much mechanical energy is converted to thermal energy between the top and the bottom, in joules?

mistakes.why: Value: that is the kinetic energy at the bottom. Subtract it from the mechanical energy at the top.
Value: that is the loss from the top to the middle only.

items.q: For which system is the total energy constant as the skier goes down the slope?
options: Skier + Earth, since friction from the snow is internal
Skier alone, since the skier's kinetic energy stays the same
No system, because energy is lost to friction on the slope
Skier + Earth + snow, since friction is then an internal force

items.q: The skier travels 50.0 m along the slope from top to bottom. If all the thermal energy came from kinetic friction, what was the average friction force, in newtons?

mistakes.why: Value: that divides the final kinetic energy by the distance. Use the energy turned into thermal energy, 3090 J.

items.q: Which bar chart matches the cart-spring system at the instant of greatest compression?
options: The U_s bar holds the energy; K is zero
K and U_s are equal
The K bar holds the energy; U_s is zero
Both K and U_s are zero, because the cart has stopped

items.q: At the instant the spring is compressed by half its greatest compression, how do K and U_s compare?
options: K and U_s are equal
K is three times U_s
U_s is three times K
K is twice U_s

items.q: What is the greatest compression of the spring, in meters?

mistakes.why: Value: you dropped the ½ from ½kx². Both sides have a ½, so they cancel: x = v√(m/k).

items.q: Now take the cart alone as the system. Which describes its energy while it compresses the spring?
options: Its total energy stays the same, now partly stored as U_s
Its kinetic energy decreases because friction does negative work
Its K decreases, because the spring (external) does negative work on it
Its kinetic energy stays the same until the spring is fully compressed and stops it

items.q: A block slides down a frictionless ramp. Which is the best justification that the mechanical energy of the block-Earth system stays constant?
options: Mechanical energy is constant because energy is conserved
The block's speed stays constant as it slides down the ramp
Gravity does no work on the block, since the ramp supports it
No friction acts, and the normal force is perpendicular to the motion, so it does no work

items.q: A roller coaster car passes over a 30.0 m high hill at 4.00 m/s. Friction is negligible. How fast is it moving when it is 10.0 m above the ground? Use g = 9.8 m/s².

mistakes.why: Value: you left out the kinetic energy at the top. ½mv² + mgΔy at the top includes the 4.00 m/s.
Value: speeds do not add. Add the energies: ½v_f² = ½v_i² + gΔh.

items.q: A block slides from rest down a frictionless ramp. If the ramp's height is doubled, the block's speed at the bottom becomes
options: √2 times as large
2 times as large
4 times as large
the same, if the ramp's angle is unchanged

items.q: A ball is dropped onto a floor and bounces back to a lower height. Which is the best explanation?
options: The energy was destroyed by the impact with the floor
Some mechanical energy became thermal energy and sound during the bounce
The ball lost mass during the bounce
Gravity is stronger on the way up, so the ball rises less

items.q: A crate slides down a rough ramp at constant speed. For the crate-ramp-Earth system, predict how each quantity changes.
How much work does winch X's cable do on its crate during the lift? Give the value and its unit.

mistakes.why: Value: that multiplies mass by height. Work is force times distance: the cable's force is mg = 392 N.

items.q: What is winch X's average power output to its crate? Give the value and its unit.

mistakes.why: Value: power is work divided by time, not multiplied.
Value: 12.0 s is winch Y's time. Winch X takes 6.00 s.

items.q: How do the two winches compare?
options: Same work; X's power is twice Y's
X does twice the work and has twice the power
Same work and same power, because the crates are identical
Same work; Y's power is twice X's, because Y works longer

items.q: Use P = Fv to find winch Y's power output to its crate, in watts.

mistakes.why: Value: F is the cable's force, mg = 392 N, not the mass.

items.q: Winch X lifts an 80.0 kg crate at the same 0.500 m/s. Its power output becomes
options: 4 times as large
2 times as large
the same, since the speed is the same
half as large

items.q: Who does the most work against gravity?
options: Ana, the fastest
Cy
Ben
The three do equal work, since the rise is the same

items.q: Who has the greatest average power output?
options: Ben, who does the most work
Ana alone, because she is fastest
The three are equal
Ana and Cy, equally

items.q: What is Ben's average power output, in watts?

mistakes.why: Value: that leaves out g. The force against gravity is mg.

items.q: In SI base units, the watt in which these powers are measured is
options: kg·m²/s³
kg·m²/s²
kg·m/s²
kg·m/s

items.q: A 1200 kg car speeds up from rest to 20. m/s in 8.0 s on level ground. What is the average power delivered to the car's kinetic energy, in watts?

mistakes.why: Value: that is mv/t, a force, not a power. Find ΔK = ½mv² first, then divide by the time.

items.q: A cyclist pushes forward with a 480 N force while moving at 25 m/s. What is the instantaneous power of this force, in watts?
A motor does a fixed amount of work in one third of the time it used to take. Its average power becomes
options: one third as large
3 times as large
9 times as large
unchanged, since the work is the same

items.q: A car's engine delivers a constant power to the wheels while the car speeds up on a level road. What happens to the forward force on the car as its speed increases?
options: It increases, because the car goes faster
It stays the same, because the power is constant
It decreases, because P = Fv is fixed and v grows
It drops to zero once the car is moving

items.q: A 75 W motor lifts a 5.0 kg load straight up at constant speed. How fast does the load rise, in m/s? Use g = 9.8 m/s².

mistakes.why: Value: that divides power by mass. Divide by the force, mg = 49 N: v = P/(mg).

items.q: An electricity bill charges for kilowatt-hours. What does a kilowatt-hour measure?
options: Power: the rate at which energy is used
Force: the push the electricity delivers
Speed: how fast the energy moves through the wires
Energy: one kilowatt of power for one hour, 3.6 × 10⁶ J
